context: Tech demo / data visualization hybrid: a scatter chart (salary vs. experience) rendered at 6 sizes using CSS container queries, demonstrating progressive simplification from full chart to sparkline to KPI widget.
first_impression: A well-organized gallery with a coherent colorblind-safe palette and impressive adaptive rendering, feeling deliberately designed rather than thrown together.
what_works: The Paul Tol palette (#4477AA, #EE6677, etc.) is a thoughtful, intentional choice that signals design awareness beyond schemeCategory10 defaults. Progressive disclosure is well-executed — each size tier strips elements purposefully, and the linked cross-panel hover highlighting is a sophisticated interaction touch.
what_doesnt: The bottom legend in the 380px simplified panel truncates category names to 4 characters (Engi, Desi, Sale) at 8px font — barely legible and cramped against the chart edge. The top-earner annotation in the full panel has an awkward short leader line that makes the text feel disconnected from the data point it annotates.
